scenarios.name: api-check-slack-email-alerts
scenarios.rationale: Response A meets every rubric item: ApiCheck at EVERY_1M, the statusCode and jsonBody assertions, EmailAlertChannel plus SlackAppAlertChannel (it explicitly avoids the deprecated webhook channel), and the {{ORDERS_API_TOKEN}} placeholder. Response B gets the check and token placeholder right but uses the deprecated webhook SlackAlertChannel, which the rubric specifically rules out.

scenarios.name: playwright-tests-as-monitors-safe
scenarios.rationale: Response A uses a PlaywrightCheck with playwrightConfigPath, pwTags ["@critical"] and Frequency.EVERY_15M, warns about the repeated real orders and recommends a test account, dryRun-style flags, cleanup and no real cards, and runs `checkly test --record` before deploy, while Response B builds a GitHub Actions scheduler instead of Checkly and only mentions Checkly in passing, so it misses the first and third rubric items and covers only the risk warning.

scenarios.name: ci-test-then-deploy-workflow
scenarios.rationale: A uses checkly/checkly-action@v1 with command: test and the API key, account ID and environment URL in env, and gives deploy --force, deploy --preview and the --preserve-resources note, so it covers nearly all of the rubric; B uses a raw npx checkly test run step instead of the required action, though its deploy --force and deploy --preview commands are correct.
